name: KaKyung Cho

education.school: Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT), New York

bio_short: KaKyung Cho is a Newburgh-based artist who works in ceramics and handmade objects. She has shown with Holland Tunnel Gallery from its Williamsburg years through its Newburgh exhibitions, including Earth & Spirit (2019) and Wood, Wool, Glass & Clay (2023).
bio_long: KaKyung Cho is an artist based in Newburgh, New York, who moved there from Williamsburg, Brooklyn. A 2017 studio profile by Uncommon Goods says she studied at the Fashion Institute of Technology, drew daily from early childhood, and built a small business making hand-cut soaps in geometric forms with packaging she designed herself. The profile also notes she was then taking ceramics classes. At Holland Tunnel Gallery she took part in Framed (2014), the 110-artist Stairmasters project in Williamsburg, and followed the gallery north. She showed in the Grand Opening of Holland Tunnel Newburgh in May 2018, in the 2018 holiday art sale, and in the 2019 Newburgh Open Studios. In fall 2019 she was one of the Hudson Valley ceramic artists in Earth & Spirit, with Tony Moore, Lynn Isaacson, Peter Yamaoka and Richard Lethen. In summer 2023 she exhibited in Wood, Wool, Glass & Clay, a group show about how material choices shape narrative, with Naomi Beth Gans, Romina Gonzales, Stuart Sachs, Tina Scepanovic and Jason Bauer.
practice: Ceramics and handmade, design-driven objects. The gallery grouped her with Hudson Valley ceramic artists (2019) and in a materials-focused show (2023). Her soap work uses simple geometric forms and minimal, self-designed packaging.

verification.evidence: Holland Tunnel sources consistently place her in Framed 2014 (Williamsburg) and in Newburgh shows from 2018 to 2023. NewburghNY.org lists her in the 2019 Newburgh Open Studios. The Uncommon Goods profile of a KaKyung Cho who moved from Williamsburg to Newburgh and was taking ceramics classes fits that timeline, but no source explicitly links it to the gallery.
